title: Spring SOI gave no clear added winter RONI forecast gain in 1981-2024
abstract: We tested whether spring air pressure improves next-winter relative ENSO forecasts after recent sea surface temperature is known. We used fixed NOAA CPC SOI and ERSSTv5 RONI records, earlier-year linear fits and 44 test winters in 1981-2024. Adding mean March-May SOI to spring RONI and its change since winter raised mean squared error by 1.68%. The conditional 95% five-year block interval for error reduction was -5.81% to +2.23%. Root mean squared error rose from 0.9046 to 0.9122 C. All seven model or scoring checks also gave intervals that included zero. This extends prior monthly pressure and spring relative-index tests to a fixed spring issue and winter target. It does not show that atmospheric information has no forecast value. Revised indices, fixed reference periods, rounded values, simple models, 44 winters and conditional uncertainty limit the result. The package gives code, source hashes, annual loss aggregates, all scores, numerical audits and a figure. Raw sources and record tables remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Added SOI MSE reduction and conditional 95% five-year block intervals. All intervals include zero. Primary and most checks use 44 winters; recent targets use 25 and omitted large targets use 41.
